title: What faculty qualifications does the Higher Learning Commission require?
description: What HLC Assumed Practice B.2 and Core Component 3.C require of faculty qualifications, how equivalent experience works, and what reviewers expect.
shortAnswer: The Higher Learning Commission (HLC) requires every accredited institution to establish and maintain reasonable policies and procedures to determine that faculty are qualified, under Assumed Practice B.2.a, and to have the faculty and staff needed for effective programs, under Core Component 3.C. HLC's September 2025 guidelines define qualification through academic credentials, progress toward credentials, or equivalent experience, and apply to every instructor, including adjunct and dual credit faculty.
keyTakeaways: Assumed Practice B.2.a (policy CRRT.C.10.010) makes the institution responsible for codified, consistently applied policies that determine faculty are qualified, covering all instructors and any other entity it assigns to teach.

Core Component 3.C, in the Criteria for Accreditation effective September 2025, requires the faculty and staff needed for effective, high quality programs and student services. Comprehensive evaluations must write specifically to it.
HLC's guidelines define achievement of academic credentials as a relevant degree at least one level above the level taught, typically a master's degree for general education courses.
Qualification through progress toward credentials is temporary, and years of classroom teaching alone do not count as equivalent experience.
Assumed Practices are treated as facts that must be met at all times; noncompliance can lead to monitoring, Probation, a Show-Cause Order or adverse action.
appliesTo: Colleges and universities accredited by, or seeking candidacy with, the Higher Learning Commission
All instructors: full time, part time, adjunct, dual credit, temporary, non-tenure-track and graduate assistants
Contractual, consortial and dual enrollment partners and subsidiaries to which an institution assigns instruction
Chief academic officers, deans and faculty committees that set and apply qualification criteria

sections.heading: Where do HLC's faculty qualification requirements come from?

blocks.text: HLC sets faculty qualification requirements in two policies: the Assumed Practices, which institutions must meet at all times, and the Criteria for Accreditation, which peer reviewers evaluate using professional judgment. HLC publishes [Institutional Policies and Procedures for Determining Faculty Qualifications](https://download.hlcommission.org/FacultyGuidelines_OPB.pdf) (September 2025) to explain both.

The [Assumed Practices](https://www.hlcommission.org/accreditation/policies/assumed-practices/) are policy CRRT.C.10.010 (formerly CRRT.B.10.020, renumbered in June 2023). HLC describes them as "generally matters to be determined as facts, rather than matters requiring professional judgment" that do not vary by mission. The policy history records a revision in June 2024 effective September 2025, a further revision in November 2025, and an edit in February 2026.

The [Criteria for Accreditation](https://www.hlcommission.org/accreditation/policies/criteria/) are policy CRRT.B.10.010, last revised in June 2024 with effect from September 2025. Criterion 3, Teaching and Learning for Student Success, contains Core Component 3.C, Sufficiency of Faculty and Staff.

Federal law shapes this structure. Under [34 CFR 602.16(a)(1)(iii)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-34/section-602.16), an accrediting agency seeking recognition from the Secretary of Education must have standards that set clear expectations for faculty. Section 602.16(g)(4) allows separate faculty standards for dual or concurrent enrollment and career and technical education instructors, provided they are qualified by education or work experience in the agency's judgment.

blocks.title: Currency
blocks.text: This page reflects HLC policy as at November 2026. The eCFR text of 34 CFR 602.16 cross references an amendment published at 91 FR 68720 on October 30, 2026; check whether it changes paragraph (a) before relying on the federal summary above.

sections.heading: What does Assumed Practice B.2 require?

blocks.text: Assumed Practice B.2 requires reasonable, institution-wide policies for determining that faculty are qualified, and substantial faculty participation in academic oversight. It has two parts.

**B.2.a** states that the institution "establishes and maintains reasonable policies and procedures to determine that faculty are qualified." The factors may include, but are not limited to, the achievement of academic credentials, progress toward academic credentials, equivalent experience or a combination. The obligation extends to all instructors and all other entities to which the institution assigns instruction.
**B.2.b** requires faculty to participate substantially in four areas:

items: Oversight of the curriculum, including its development, vetting, implementation, academic substance, currency and relevance.
Assurance of consistency in the level and quality of instruction and in expectations of student performance.
Establishment of qualifications for instructors, including instructors provided by third parties.
Analysis of data and appropriate action on assessment of student learning and program completion.

blocks.text: Item three matters for training design: faculty, not only administrators, should help write the qualification criteria. HLC's guidelines repeat that faculty "should participate substantially in the establishment of institutional policies and procedures for faculty qualifications."

sections.heading: How does HLC define a qualified instructor?

blocks.text: HLC accepts three routes to qualification, each defined in its guidelines, and expects the institution's policy to be codified, transparent, consistently implemented and regularly reviewed.

blocks.caption: HLC's three qualification routes as defined in the September 2025 guidelines
head: Route
What HLC's guidelines say
Practical consequence
rows: Achievement of academic credentials

A degree relevant to the subject and at least one level above the level taught; in terminal degree programs, the same level of degree. For general education and other non-occupational courses, typically a master's degree or higher, generally in the discipline.
If the degree is in another discipline, the instructor needs a reasonable amount of coursework in the teaching discipline, as defined by the institution.
Progress toward academic credentials
Demonstrable, current and consistent progress toward the credential the institution deems relevant.
Not permanent: the instructor is expected eventually to qualify on another basis, and must have access to teaching support such as professional development or collaboration with qualified faculty.
Equivalent experience
Experience commensurate with the credential, which may include a minimum threshold of experience, research or scholarship, or recognized achievement, and may differ by discipline.
Previous years of classroom instruction do not alone constitute equivalent experience.

blocks.text: The guidelines apply to instructors only. Institutions must determine appropriate qualifications for other staff, and HLC states its requirements are "in no way a mandate" to make any personnel decision.

Core Component 3.C adds a sufficiency test: "The institution has the faculty and staff needed for effective, high-quality programs and student services." Qualified individuals are not enough if there are too few of them for the programs and modalities offered.

HLC's guidelines say 3.C addresses a faculty member's ability to understand and convey the essentials of a discipline, engage with colleagues on learning objectives for graduates, and stay aware of student learning through the collection and analysis of data. Criterion 3 also requires consistent rigor and quality "regardless of modality, location or other differentiating factors," which brings online and dual credit sections into scope.

HLC's [Providing Evidence for the Criteria](https://download.hlcommission.org/ProvidingEvidence-2025Criteria_INF.pdf) resource lists examples for 3.C, including the qualification policies and procedures, student to faculty ratios overall and by modality, hiring guidelines for each faculty type, orientation materials for all faculty, professional development plans and annual evaluations, and data that led to policy changes.

Business schools that also hold programmatic accreditation face a stricter, numeric version of the same test: see [AACSB faculty qualification and assurance of learning standards](/regulations/aacsb-assurance-of-learning-standard). For the wider sector context, see [higher education](/industries/higher-education).

HLC reviews the institution's qualification system, not each faculty file. Its guidelines state that peer reviewers "are not expected to evaluate the individual qualifications of specific faculty members"; if they identify systemic noncompliance, they seek more information and may recommend follow-up.

items: **Comprehensive evaluations:** institutions must write specifically to Core Component 3.C. On routine Standard or Open Pathway comprehensive evaluations they need not write to the Assumed Practices.
**Candidacy and initial accreditation:** institutions must evidence compliance with all Assumed Practices.
**Probation and Show-Cause:** institutions must evidence compliance with the cited Assumed Practices (Probation) or all of them (Show-Cause) to have the sanction removed.
**Complaints:** HLC may request documentation on Assumed Practice compliance through its complaints process.

blocks.text: The stakes are explicit in the Assumed Practices policy: an institution out of compliance with any Assumed Practice, even if it meets every other requirement, may be subject to monitoring, Probation, a Show-Cause Order or an adverse action, depending on the gravity of the finding.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry treats each course's learning outcomes as the reference point for qualification decisions, so an equivalent experience judgment can be tested against what the course actually requires rather than against years in a role. The same outcome map supports the assessment data faculty analyze under B.2.b and the sufficiency evidence for Core Component 3.C.

faqs.q: Does HLC set a minimum number of graduate credit hours in the teaching discipline?
faqs.a: HLC's September 2025 guidelines do not set a credit hour figure. Where an instructor's degree is in a different discipline, they must have completed a reasonable amount of coursework in the teaching discipline "as defined by the institution." The institution sets the threshold in its codified policy and must apply it consistently.

faqs.q: Do HLC faculty qualification rules apply to dual credit instructors?
faqs.a: Yes. HLC's guidelines list dual credit instructors among the categories covered, and the Assumed Practice extends to all entities to which the institution assigns instruction, including dual enrollment partners. HLC also maintains separate Dual Credit Guidelines, and federal rules allow accreditors to set separate faculty standards for dual enrollment courses.

faqs.q: Can teaching experience count as equivalent experience?
faqs.a: Not on its own. HLC's guidelines state that previous years of classroom instruction do not alone constitute equivalent experience. Equivalent experience must be commensurate with the academic credential and may include a minimum threshold of professional experience, research or scholarship, or recognized achievement.

faqs.q: Will HLC peer reviewers inspect individual faculty files?
faqs.a: Normally not. HLC's guidelines say peer reviewers evaluate the institution's policies and procedures and are not expected to evaluate the qualifications of specific faculty members. If a team finds systemic noncompliance, it seeks further information and may recommend HLC follow-up.

B.2.a requires reasonable policies and procedures to determine faculty are qualified (credentials, progress, equivalent experience or combination), extending to all instructors and other entities assigned instruction; B.2.b lists four areas of substantial faculty participation
Noncompliance with any Assumed Practice may lead to monitoring, Probation, a Show-Cause Order or adverse action; evidence required at candidacy, initial accreditation, Probation and Show-Cause

Criteria for Accreditation policy CRRT.B.10.010 revised June 2024 effective September 2025; Core Component 3.C: the institution has the faculty and staff needed for effective, high-quality programs and student services

Guidelines (September 2025): requirements apply to full-time, part-time, adjunct, dual credit, temporary, non-tenure-track, graduate assistant instructors; credential means degree at least one level above level taught, typically master's for general education; reasonable coursework as defined by institution; progress toward credentials not permanent; classroom years alone not equivalent experience

Peer reviewers are not expected to evaluate individual faculty qualifications; comprehensive evaluations must write specifically to 3.C; routine Standard or Open Pathway comprehensive evaluations need not write to Assumed Practices
3.C evidence examples include qualification policies, student to faculty ratios by modality, hiring guidelines, orientation materials, professional development plans and annual evaluations

34 CFR 602.16(a)(1)(iii) requires agency standards on faculty; 602.16(g)(4) permits separate faculty standards for dual or concurrent enrollment and CTE instructors; eCFR cross references an amendment at 91 FR 68720, Oct. 30, 2026
